content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble connecting my module to the Internet and using GPS. While I can make calls and send SMS, I'm unable to send emails or access the module via HTTPS through the web interface. I have all necessary antennas (GPS - [product_name], GSM - Unknown) with signal strength at 28/-57dBm, but no data is transmitted or received. GPS appears enabled, but the module does not detect any satellites. I'm using a SIM card from Play that works on my phone (2G tested), with APN set to "internet." Error message: "Sending e-mail failed. Last reply from server 0. Internal error identifier: 7. Number of attempts: 1." Looking for assistance to enable Internet and activate GPS functionality.

Hello, Mobile Data and GPS typically operate separately, so each may have a different issue. For GPS, is your antenna installed inside or outside? From my experience, GPS does not work reliably indoors; an outdoor placement is necessary. The email error "Last reply from server 0. Internal error identifier: 7" suggests that there's no connection to the mail server, which may stem from several causes. Please review diagnostics and WAN status: - Is the [product_name] module connected to mobile data? If not, email will fail until this is resolved. - If mobile data is connected but the error persists, check your configured SMTP address. Regarding HTTPS web interface access, you must activate this feature and possess a publicly accessible IP from your provider. Most standard mobile IPs are not reachable from the Internet unless you have a specific contract/APN for public access. Best regards, [user_name]

I will relocate the [product_name] module and test GPS outdoors. The module has mobile data enabled. To send emails, I created an account on [url]. I verified SMTP server name and port settings, but it still doesn't work. I'm not sure what the issue is, but I will proceed with GPS testing now.

GPS is now functioning. I'm surprised at how sensitive this antenna is.
You're currently using port 465 for email. Try switching to port 587, which is more commonly used for SMTP.

It works now. I changed the SMTP port as suggested and enabled SMTP settings on my email account. Unfortunately, I couldn't find a similar setting for Gmail, only IMAP and POP were available. Thank you for the support. Next, I will set up HTTP and prepare to add the [product_name] module to my plant setup.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered persistent issues connecting a [product_name] module to the Internet, preventing email transmission and reliable GPS reception. The module initially failed to detect satellites, and email configuration attempts resulted in vague system errors. Through community suggestions, the user discovered that antenna placement critically impacts GPS performance and that proper SMTP port selection resolves email issues. Error feedback from the system was insufficient, so users relied on trial, error, and advice from others to address configuration problems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek straightforward step-by-step setup for email and GPS connectivity, detailed and helpful error messages for troubleshooting, and dependable operation with default hardware and configuration per documentation.
